title: Steven Lovekin: Eisenhower doodled UFOs at Mount Weather, UFO headquarters
summary: Grant Cameron tells of Steven Lovekin: Eisenhower doodled UFOs at Mount Weather, UFO headquarters, about 1950s at Mount Weather, Virginia, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: to him about being inside Mount Weather with with uh Eisenhower and he he said Eisenhower would doodle UFO stuff and that sort of stuff and that Eisenhower was this is where UFOs were headquartered.

related.note: Both are Lovekin's testimony that Eisenhower doodled UFO craft. This telling puts it at Mount Weather as UFO headquarters; the story has it at the White House, with Eisenhower saying he no longer controlled the issue.

plain: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says he spoke with Steven Lovekin, a man who says he was inside Mount Weather, a government site in Virginia, with President Dwight Eisenhower in the 1950s. According to Cameron, Lovekin said Eisenhower used to doodle UFO drawings there, and that Mount Weather was where the UFO matter was headquartered. If true, it would put the president personally close to the subject.
